value: touch genes TCH3, TCH4, CML24 and CML39 induced 0.5 to 1 h after soft mechanical stimulation (10 successive rubbings)
units: transcript induction (qPCR; direction only in text)
method: leaves of A. thaliana Col-0 gently rubbed between thumb and forefinger without pressing; touch-gene transcripts by qPCR (reference gene At4g26410) in untreated and soft-mechanical-stimulation (SMS) leaves
conditions: Col-0 wild type; 12 h photoperiod, 21/19 C, 100 uE, 60 to 70% RH; T-test at p < 0.05; time course run at 1, 5 and 7 times SMS; SMS repeated 10 successive times for Figure 2C; qPCR n = 3 (mean ± SD), repeated three times with similar results; no force measured; plant age for the qPCR not captured (inoculated leaves came from 4-week-old plants, cameleon imaging used 16 to 21-day-old plants). The text gives no fold changes (they are in Figure 2C) and reports no touch gene among these four as not induced. The same paper reports the induced resistance to Botrytis cinerea was transient (about half lost when inoculated 8 h after SMS, fully susceptible at 24 h) and that SMS was followed by a rapid change in intracellular calcium (cameleon and aequorin lines, transgenic reporters).

units: degrees (petiole angle to the horizontal, approximate)
method: an inert transparent tag placed gently in the soil beside the fifth-youngest leaf to mimic leaf-leaf contact; petiole angle measured in ImageJ at 0 h and 24 h
conditions: Col-0 wild type, 28-day-old plants; short-day growth (9 h/15 h, 130 to 135 umol, R:FR 2.3, 20 C, 70% RH); force not quantified (described as gentle, much weaker than wounding); n = 7 biological replicates for Fig. 1a, c; two-way ANOVA with Tukey's test or unpaired t test, p < 0.05; untouched control group.
